title: Baked Salmon
subtitle: Simple oven-baked salmon with lemon and herbs
excerpt: Salmon fillets baked in the oven with lemon, olive oil, and dill until just set through. The most straightforward way to cook salmon. On the table in 20 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Baking salmon in the oven is the most reliable method for home cooks: the temperature is controlled, there is no oil splatter, and the fish does not require attention during cooking. The salmon is done when it turns from translucent to opaque throughout, or when it flakes with a fork. The interior should be just set; pink is fine at the centre. Overcooked salmon goes dry and chalky.

recipeTools.notes: Lined with foil for easy cleaning.

content.text: Take the salmon out of the fridge 15 minutes before cooking: a cold fillet takes longer to cook through and risks an overcooked exterior with a cold centre. The salmon is done when the flesh has turned from deep translucent pink to a paler, more opaque pink throughout. A probe thermometer at the thickest part should read 52 to 55 C for a just-set, moist result.

items.preparation: skin-on, about 150 g each, at room temperature
half sliced into rounds, half for juice

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Line a baking tray with foil. Arrange the lemon slices on the tray. Place the salmon fillets skin-side down on top of the lemon.
Drizzle the olive oil over the salmon. Scatter over the garlic slices. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes depending on thickness, until the salmon is just opaque throughout. The flesh should flake when pressed with a fork.
Squeeze the juice from the remaining lemon half over the fillets. Scatter with dill. Serve with new potatoes and a green salad.
